prs.title: Normative: Update RevalidateAtomicAccess to account for all bytes of a TypedArray element
prs.author: gibson042
prs.body:
Fixes #3924
Ref #3200

When a length-tracking TypedArray has multi-byte elements (e.g., Int32Array or BigInt64Array) and its backing ArrayBuffer is shrunk during Atomics function argument coercion so a target element that was previously in bounds now _starts_ in bounds but extends past the new shorter _end_, revalidation must fail in order to avoid control reaching a "sufficient bytes in arrayBuffer" assertion that fails.

```js
const rab = new ArrayBuffer(12, { maxByteLength: 12 });
const ta = new Int32Array(rab); // length-tracking; element 1 spans byte indices 4..7
Atomics.and(ta, 1, { valueOf() { rab.resize(7); return 1; } });
```

test262 PR: https://github.com/tc39/test262/pull/5106
Consistent with current conforming/nonconforming behavior for shrinking a backing ArrayBuffer by a _whole_ number of elements, JavaScriptCore and V8 fail only by incorrectly throwing TypeError rather than RangeError when the TypedArray is length-tracking and Moddable XS fails by incorrectly proceeding without throwing exceptions at all.

prs.title: Editorial: Clean up some numeric literal text
prs.author: gibson042
prs.body:
* In MV clauses, consistently use "×" and "+" rather than "times" and "plus"
* Replace `0` and |NonZeroDigit| alternative productions with |DecimalDigit|
* Simplify the |NonOctalDecimalIntegerLiteral| grammar (_consolidate the mandatory leading `0` and merge the non-recursive cases, aligning with |LegacyOctalIntegerLiteral| to better highlight the differences_)
* Use a smaller example to explain "one of"
